chunks: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said to one of his companions:
Do not reveal to your friend any of your secrets except what would cause you no harm if your enemy were to learn of it, for indeed a friend may become an enemy one day.

key_terms.الصَّادِق: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), the sixth Shia Imam, renowned for his vast scholarship and teaching
key_terms.سِرّ: secret; a private matter not meant for disclosure
key_terms.عَدُوّ: enemy; an adversary who may seek to cause harm

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about sharing secrets with friends?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a practical and cautious maxim about the limits of disclosure even within close friendships: only share secrets that would be harmless if a hostile party were to discover them. The wisdom here acknowledges the impermanence of human relationships — a trusted friend today may one day become an adversary. This teaching reflects the broader Islamic ethical principle of prudence (hikmah) in managing personal affairs and protecting one's vulnerabilities.
